What is ChatGPT?

General-purpose conversational assistant built on OpenAI's GPT model family. Handles open-ended dialogue, reasoning, document and image analysis, code generation, web-grounded research and agentic task execution from a single chat surface.

Best for

Broad daily knowledge work where one assistant must cover writing, analysis and code.

Main features

  • Multimodal input (text, image, file, voice)
  • Deep Research
  • Advanced Voice Mode
  • Canvas collaborative editor
  • Custom GPTs and GPT Store
  • Projects and memory
  • Codex coding agent
  • Sora video generation on top tiers
  • connectors to Drive/SharePoint/GitHub.

Practical use cases

  • Drafting and editing documents
  • summarising long PDFs and reports
  • brainstorming
  • translation
  • data analysis on uploaded spreadsheets
  • coding help and debugging
  • customer-facing copy
  • market and competitive research.

Who is it for?

  • Everyone from casual consumers to knowledge workers, developers, students and enterprise teams.

Pricing, free access & limits

Freemium subscription; per-seat for business; separate token-metered API

Plans described in the source

Free $0 (ad-supported since the 2026 ad rollout). Go $8/mo. Plus $20/mo. Pro sold as two usage tiers: $100/mo (5x Plus usage) and $200/mo (20x Plus usage, priority compute, ~250 Deep Research tasks). Business $20/seat/mo annual or $25/seat/mo monthly (2-seat minimum; cut from $25/$30 in April 2026); a Premium seat runs roughly $100-125. Enterprise custom, annual contract. API billed per token, separate bill.

Free plan

Yes - permanent free tier with unlimited everyday text chat, but ad-supported and with separate caps on uploads, images, voice and research.

Free trial

No standalone free trial of Plus/Pro; the free tier serves that purpose. Business trials are handled through sales.

Usage limits to consider

Free and Go have capped uploads, image generation, voice, deep research and memory. Plus uses a rolling message cap resetting every few hours plus a weekly cap on extended-reasoning messages. Pro is 'unlimited subject to abuse guardrails' with no published cap. Context tops out around 128K instant / 400K reasoning tokens on Pro.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Largest feature surface of any consumer assistant
  • strongest third-party ecosystem
  • excellent multimodal handling
  • agentic Codex and Operator tooling
  • mature enterprise controls on Business/Enterprise.

Limitations to consider

  • Pricing tiers are confusing (two plans both badged 'Pro')
  • free and Go tiers now carry ads
  • consumer plans train on your data by default unless you opt out
  • message caps interrupt heavy sessions on Plus
  • model routing is not shown to the user.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web, Windows, macOS, iOS, Android
  • Chrome/Edge extensions
  • Atlas browser

Languages

  • 50+ conversational languages including Arabic, French and English; UI localised in a smaller set

API access

Yes - OpenAI Platform API, token-metered and billed separately from ChatGPT plans

Integrations and exports

  • Google Drive, OneDrive/SharePoint, GitHub, Slack, Gmail, Outlook, Box, Zapier
  • MCP connectors
  • custom GPT actions

Evaluation notes

Rollout of new models varies by account, region and plan, so two users on the same tier may see different models. Business/Enterprise exclude training on your data by default; consumer tiers require a settings change.
